free_tier.stated: No account, no quota, no total cap stated — 'Free and unrestricted... with no warranties... for now.' Per-file 100 MiB. First person to upload an object owns it (SHA-256 addressed).

retention.stated: 100 MiB/file; files deleted if not accessed for 60 days; /list returns only the first 250 hits; BUD-08 (NIP-94) not implemented

egress.terms: free, unauthenticated GET by SHA-256; served from a public host with no metering published

interface_detail: BUD-01 HTTP: PUT /upload (NIP-98 auth header), GET /<sha256>, HEAD /upload for BUD-06 pre-flight, /mirror for BUD-06
tooling: any Blossom client (nostr.build, ditto, Amethyst); `nak` for key generation; plain curl once you can sign a NIP-98 event
chaining: Content-addressed means a chunk map is trivial: `(sha256 → server)` is a complete locator, and BUD-06 /mirror lets one server pull a blob from another — so replication is a one-request operation per chunk.

limits.value: deleted if not accessed for 60 days

limits_note: 100 MiB/file; files deleted if not accessed for 60 days; /list returns only the first 250 hits; BUD-08 (NIP-94) not implemented

identity_cost.detail: anonymous — a Nostr keypair is the credential; no email, no phone. Verified: HEAD /upload with a BUD-06 pre-flight but no auth header returns 401 'x-reason: Authorization header missing, when required'.

reliability_note: 60-day access-decay retention makes this an ephemeral tier, not an archive. 100 MiB/file means ~5,000 objects per 500 GB.

evidence.proved: 'Max file size: 100MiB'; 'Files are deleted if not accessed for 60 days'; 'First person to upload an object owns it'; BUD-06 /mirror accepts only another blossom URL

HEAD — 401, X-Reason: 'This needs a Nostr auth token (BUD-11)'
